paper_title: Strong constraints on decay and annihilation of dark matter from heating of gas-rich dwarf galaxies
notes: Paper constrains axion-like particles (ALPs) decaying to photons via gas heating in the Leo T dwarf galaxy. The primary constraint comes from requiring DM decay/annihilation heating rate to not exceed the ultra-low radiative cooling rate of neutral hydrogen gas in Leo T. For ALPs, the decay rate Γ_a = m_a^3 g_agamma^2 / (64π) is used to convert lifetime bounds to g_agamma constraints. The paper reports Leo T provides the best limit on ALP-photon coupling for m_a ~ 30 eV–keV (Fig. 4). Data points extracted from Fig. 4 (black curve, Leo T gas temp. = 6100 K). The bounds are strongest in the 30 eV–1 keV range where direct photon background measurements are weakest (extreme UV range). This is a model-dependent constraint derived from the model-independent decay lifetime bounds shown in Fig. 3 (top right panel: χ → γγ). The paper also discusses constraints on other DM models (sterile neutrinos, Higgs portal scalars, dark baryons, excited DM states) but the ALP-photon coupling is the most directly comparable to standard axion searches. | selector: text (sole candidate)
